D005-D006_h001.question:

I’ve been having a really hard time for about three months now. At first I thought it was just burnout from the hospice, but it’s…different. I keep having this feeling that everything is about to end, like there’s some kind of collapse coming. When I’m with my patients, I catch myself thinking, “What’s the point of morphine or comfort if the whole world is about to be wiped out?” It doesn’t feel like a worry; it feels like a fact I just can’t shake.

On top of that, I sometimes feel things crawling or brushing against my skin—like fingers tapping my arms or something moving along my legs—when there’s nothing there. It happens at work and at home. I keep checking my clothes, the bed, but there’s never anything.

My mood and energy have been all over the place. There are stretches where I barely sleep and feel strangely wired and driven, talking more, taking on extra shifts, starting projects at night. Then other times I just freeze up. People at work will tell me to do something simple, and I just stare or do the opposite without really meaning to, like I’m pushing back automatically or can’t make myself respond.

    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D006_h023.question:
I guess this all really started around three months ago. At first I thought it was just burnout from the booth, but it’s gotten…strange. I keep having this fixed sense that something is wrong inside my body, like my organs are rotting or rearranged. I’ve had blood work, scans, everything comes back “normal,” but it doesn’t feel normal. I keep checking my skin, my mouth, my abdomen, but I can’t shake the idea that something is fundamentally damaged.

On top of that, I taste things that aren’t there. It can be in the middle of interpreting a conference call and suddenly there’s this metallic, almost chemical flavor in my mouth, or something sickly sweet, even when I’m just drinking water. No one else tastes it, and it makes me lose my train of thought.

My mood has been all over the place, but not in a way I can easily pin down. There are days I feel unusually wired, talking fast, jumping between projects, sleeping less because I “don’t need it,” and then it sort of settles back down. I can’t tell how long those phases last; they blend into the rest of this.

My colleagues have commented that I sit very still, and when people move my arm or adjust my posture I just…let them. It’s like my body goes along with it and I feel oddly detached, almost like I’m being posed rather than moving on my own.

    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h024.question:
I’ve been feeling like something terrible is about to happen for about three months now. It’s not just anxiety… it’s like this certainty that everything is coming apart, like the world is winding down and any day now there’s going to be some huge disaster. When I’m on the line at night, I’ll catch myself thinking, “What’s the point of packing all this if nothing’s going to be here soon?”

Around the same time, I started hearing this voice, usually when it’s quiet or I’m trying to sleep after my shift. It’s not my own thoughts. It’s like someone standing just behind me, sometimes calling my name, sometimes saying things like “It’s all ending” or “You can’t stop it.” I look around but no one’s there.

People at work have asked if I’m okay because I guess my face will twist up or I’ll make weird expressions without noticing, especially when the voice gets loud. Lately I’ve also had these bursts where I feel wired and restless, like I’ve had a ton of energy even though I barely sleep. I talk faster, my thoughts race, and I feel like I need to keep moving or starting new things, but it doesn’t last the whole time—sometimes it fades and I’m just left with the voice and that feeling that everything’s doomed.

    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005-D006_h025.question:
I guess the main thing is this constant feeling that something is really wrong inside my body. For about three months now, I’ve been convinced there’s… I don’t know, some kind of infestation or growth under my skin or in my organs that no one’s finding. I’ve had tests, they say everything is normal, but it doesn’t feel normal. It feels like something is moving inside me.

Sometimes I actually feel things crawling or wriggling on my arms, across my back, like tiny bugs or threads under the skin. When I look, there’s nothing there, but the feeling is so real it makes it hard to sit still, especially when I’m trying to do paperwork or meet with a client.

There are days where I just stop talking. At work or at home, I’ll know what I want to say, but it’s like my mouth won’t cooperate and I just… shut down. My coworkers think I’m “spacing out,” but I’m very aware, just unable or unwilling to respond.

On and off during these months, I’ve also had times when I feel unusually driven and wired—sleeping less, talking more than usual, taking on too many cases—then it sort of fades, and I’m back to this strange, quiet, uncomfortable state.

A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
